verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser is a cloud SaaS that handles user browsing data, recordings, and AI-driven extraction, so a training-data opt-out is a fair privacy question for it. Nothing in the evidence pack mentions a training-data policy, a no-training commitment, or an opt-out control. The robots.txt and scraping complaints concern how it treats third-party sites, not whether customer data trains models, so they are not relevant here.
